retouchGenerator.scope: The Hermit and Temperance only, after precision ImageGen edits were rejected for redrawing material outside the reviewed star footprint.

prompt.shared: Quiet Celestial Storybook tarot illustration for one coherent 78-card deck, warm hand-painted gouache and delicate ink texture on aged paper, natural age-appropriate five-to-six-head human proportions, expressive non-glossy faces, correct natural hands and limbs, one coherent physical scene, restrained dusty blue, indigo, plum, cream, ochre, moss and small antique-gold accents, varied but natural light, a clear card-specific focal silhouette occupying roughly twenty to thirty-five percent of the portrait, designed for an exact 5:7 crop, no border and no text.
prompt.negative: No title, numeral, caption, lettering, watermark, logo, signature, ornate card frame, photorealism, glossy 3D, chibi anatomy, oversized head, extra fingers, fused hands, duplicate person, duplicated suit object, incorrect suit-object count, floating icon collage, neon glow, glitter, heart decoration, gore, explicit injury, horror spectacle, or candy-color gradient.

referencePolicy.instruction: Use the supplied approved anchors only for palette, natural body proportion, gouache-and-ink material, recurring character identity and world continuity. Do not copy an anchor's composition, pose, dominant symbol or incidental objects into the new card.

referenceResolution.legacySeedReferenceIdsScope: Retouch targets, replacement/new Major Arcana, and the 16 pilots only. The field never controls a non-pilot Minor Arcana prompt.
referenceResolution.nonPilotMinorOverride: The two approved promoted v3 suit anchors in generationPlan.plannedSuitAnchorIds always replace legacySeedReferenceIds.
referenceResolution.retouchedLegacyRule: The v2 source is usable only while editing that same retouch target. Every other card resolves this ID to its independently approved v3 retouch asset and final SHA.

generationPlan.postPilotReferencePolicy: Every non-pilot Minor Arcana prompt must use the two independently approved and explicitly promoted v3 anchors for its own suit, overriding that card's legacySeedReferenceIds. A planned anchor ID is not usable until its approval record locks the final JPEG SHA and marks it promotedSuitAnchor.
finalDeckGateChecks: all card identities legible at thumbnail size
no repeated scene or signature silhouette
exact suit-object counts across the full deck
natural anatomy and safe difficult-card treatment

compositionRules: Reserve each Major Arcana signature silhouette for that card; do not reuse a large star, sun, moon, wheel, scales, lion, tower, or chariot as decoration elsewhere.
Use paths and water only when the card direction requires them, not as default symbols for every abstract idea.
Vary interior and exterior space, season, weather, elevation, camera distance, and figure scale while preserving the same world materials and rendering.
Allow fatigue, grief, conflict, vigilance, surprise, and sober attention; do not make every figure smile.
Do not repeatedly assign authority, danger, passivity, poverty, or distress to one ethnicity, gender presentation, age group, or disability.
A numbered Minor Arcana card must contain exactly the specified count of its suit object, with no similar background props that make the count ambiguous.
A court card expresses a role through observable action, never merely through assumed age or gender.
Every book, map, plan, charter, decision sheet, notebook, record or document must be blank with no visible letters, words, numerals, pseudo-writing or decorative marks.

rankRules.ace: One suit object is the dominant focus and introduces potential without a floating disembodied hand.
rankRules.2-10: Show exactly the rank number of suit objects as physical parts of one readable scene.
rankRules.page: A learner or explorer studies one suit object with open curiosity.
rankRules.knight: A moving steward carries one suit object into action; the four Knights must use different movement and camera angles.
rankRules.queen: A composed steward tends, understands, or coordinates one suit object; do not rely on gender, a crown, or a throne.
rankRules.king: A responsible steward decides, protects, or operates a system using one suit object; do not rely on gender, a crown, or a throne.

wands.object: a straight, bark-textured wooden staff from one consistent family
wands.palette: sunlit ochre, plum, warm moss and dry grass
wands.environment: high dry hills, a workshop yard, traveler camps and community gathering grounds
wands.avoid: No decorative branches, fence posts, poles, or Magician-style brass wand that could change the exact staff count.

cups.object: one consistent family of handled ceramic cups with a thin antique-gold rim
cups.palette: dusty blue, teal, cream and restrained indigo
cups.environment: waterside homes, shared tables, courtyards, riverbanks and coast paths
cups.avoid: No extra bowls, mugs or vases that resemble cups; no pouring-between-vessels pose reserved for Temperance and The Star.

swords.object: one consistent family of simple straight steel swords
swords.palette: blue gray, indigo, silver and winter cream
swords.environment: windy high terraces, quiet rooms, bridges, winter roads and open plains
swords.avoid: No blood, penetrating wounds, corpses or graphic violence; no knives or tools that can be mistaken for extra swords.

pentacles.object: one consistent family of round wood-and-brass disks engraved with a single five-point mark
pentacles.palette: moss, ochre, brown, cream and muted gold
pentacles.environment: fields, markets, workshops, home gardens, store rooms and civic work sites
pentacles.avoid: No coins, buttons, plates or decorative stars that can be mistaken for extra pentacles.

difficultCardSafety.death: Show unmistakable ending and transition without predicting literal death, a corpse, gore or explicit injury.
difficultCardSafety.the-devil: Show restrictive attachment with visibly loosenable bonds; no supernatural truth claim, fetishized coercion or cute mascot treatment.
difficultCardSafety.the-tower: Show shock and structural collapse without detailed bodily harm, falling bodies or disaster spectacle.
difficultCardSafety.swords-3: Make grief legible using rain, posture and three swords against cloth or a crafted emblem; no anatomical heart, blood or penetration.
difficultCardSafety.swords-9: Show wakeful worry without diagnosing mental illness, self-harm imagery or horror figures.
difficultCardSafety.swords-10: Show exhaustion and a clear ending without a corpse, blood or swords entering a body.
difficultCardSafety.pentacles-5: Show material difficulty and exclusion without assigning poverty to one ethnicity, disability, body type or age.

cast.description: Medium-brown skin, short dark curls, open expression, plum-and-cream clothing and the same facial structure as The Fool.
Deep-brown skin, long braids with small gold details, blue-and-ochre clothing and the same facial structure as The Lovers.
Olive skin, short copper curls, green-and-cream clothing and the same facial structure as The Lovers.
Older East Asian woman with a silver bob, indigo-and-ochre clothing and the same facial structure as The Star.
A varied-age highland community with sun-worn plum, ochre and moss work clothes; distribute agency and conflict across different people.
A varied-age waterside community in dusty blue, teal and cream garments; show emotion through reciprocal actions and posture.
A varied-age highland and winter-road community in blue gray, indigo and silver-trimmed practical clothes; keep conflict non-graphic.
A varied-age field, market and workshop community in moss, ochre and brown garments; distribute skill, hardship and authority fairly.

locations.description: Connected mountain paths, orchards, cultivated fields and flowering thresholds of pale stone and aged wood.
A hilltop observatory world of moonlit library rooms, quiet courtyards and pale stone, used only when the Major direction requires it.
Warm workshops, council terraces and sheltered civic rooms using aged wood, pale stone, dusty cloth and practical tools.
Sunny high dry hills, practice yards, traveler camps and gathering grounds with broad sky and warm wind.
Waterside homes, communal tables, quiet courtyards, riverbanks and coast paths with soft reflected light.
Windy terraces, sparse rooms, bridges, open winter roads and cloud-shadowed plains with clear silhouettes.
Fields, markets, workshops, home gardens and store rooms connected by pale-stone lanes.

the-fool.name: The Fool
the-fool.gesture: The traveler takes one confident step toward an open mountain path while a small natural dog stays close.
the-fool.dominantSymbol: an open path beside a visible drop
the-fool.avoid: No large star and no wand-like walking staff; keep it distinct from Page and Knight of Wands.

the-magician.name: The Magician
the-magician.gesture: The maker stands behind a sparse worktable, one hand raising a brass wand and the other pointing down toward four clearly different suit tools.
the-magician.dominantSymbol: the above-and-below gesture beneath a loose infinity loop
supportingSymbols: exactly one wand, one cup, one sword and one pentacle
white flowers at the table edge
the-magician.avoid: No hammer, rope or extra workshop tools; do not resemble Three or Eight of Pentacles.

the-high-priestess.name: The High Priestess
the-high-priestess.gesture: The astronomer sits frontally between one dark and one pale column, holding a partly veiled closed book with a featureless cover and no visible writing or marks, in a calm listening posture.
the-high-priestess.dominantSymbol: two contrasting columns and a patterned veil
supportingSymbols: a partly hidden book with no visible writing or marks
the-high-priestess.avoid: No star chart, large sky moon, observatory dome or water channel; keep it distinct from The Moon and The Star.

the-empress.name: The Empress
the-empress.gesture: Seen from a three-quarter medium distance, the gardener stands beneath an abundant living canopy and opens one fruit-laden pomegranate branch toward neighbors arriving with gathered wheat, welcoming shared abundance rather than inspecting a crop.
the-empress.dominantSymbol: a broad living canopy with twelve small star ornaments above the welcoming gardener
the-empress.avoid: No seed basket or crop-inspection pose; do not resemble Seven or Queen of Pentacles.

the-emperor.name: The Emperor
the-emperor.gesture: Seen from a low three-quarter angle, the elder civic steward stands at a square pale-stone overlook, holding a compact staff of office while surveying a stable mountain road.
the-emperor.dominantSymbol: a square stone overlook framed by a mountain
supportingSymbols: a blank measured civic charter with no visible writing or marks
the-emperor.avoid: No model-building or workbench; do not resemble King of Pentacles or Three of Pentacles.

the-hierophant.name: The Hierophant
the-hierophant.gesture: Seen in a wide side view, the elder teacher stands at an open civic threshold, offering a teaching gesture to two attentive learners seated at different heights with distinct postures.
the-hierophant.dominantSymbol: two crossed keys laid between teacher and learners
supportingSymbols: a shared open book with completely blank pages and no visible marks
the-hierophant.avoid: No religious logo, worship claim, throne or observatory props; show guidance and shared tradition rather than obedience.

the-lovers.name: The Lovers
the-lovers.gesture: The pair face each other at a flowering threshold with mutually offered open hands and clear personal space.
the-lovers.dominantSymbol: two paths joining beneath a large warm light
the-lovers.avoid: No cups; Two of Cups must use an exchange scene rather than this open-hand composition.

the-chariot.name: The Chariot
the-chariot.gesture: The traveler stands securely in a practical wooden chariot, calmly coordinating a dark horse and a pale horse on one road.
the-chariot.avoid: No knight's single mount and no racing spectacle.

strength.name: Strength
strength.gesture: The gardener gently wraps a calm lion's injured paw while the animal freely remains near.
strength.dominantSymbol: a calm lion in voluntary contact
strength.avoid: No domination, roaring attack or other large cat anywhere else in the deck.

the-hermit.name: The Hermit
the-hermit.retouchInstruction: Remove the large eight-point star and preserve every other approved visual property; the v2 source remains byte-identical history.
the-hermit.gesture: The astronomer walks alone on a high stone path, holding a hooded lantern ahead and a plain staff in the other hand.
the-hermit.avoid: No large star and no open star chart; preserve the lantern silhouette.

wheel-of-fortune.name: Wheel of Fortune
wheel-of-fortune.gesture: The traveler pauses beside a large working waterwheel at a four-way crossing while water and changing weather continue moving.
wheel-of-fortune.avoid: No other card may feature a giant wheel or four-way crossing.

justice.name: Justice
justice.gesture: The civic adjudicator sits frontally between balanced curtains, holding level scales in one hand and a straight upright sword in the other.
justice.dominantSymbol: level scales paired with one upright sword
supportingSymbols: a plain blank decision sheet with no visible writing or marks
justice.avoid: No blindfold, courtroom logo or multiple swords; symmetry must distinguish it from Two of Swords.

the-hanged-man.name: The Hanged Man
the-hanged-man.gesture: The traveler hangs safely and voluntarily by one ankle from a living wooden frame, the free leg bent behind and hands relaxed, face calm.
the-hanged-man.dominantSymbol: the serene inverted figure and bent leg
supportingSymbols: a soft halo of dawn light
the-hanged-man.avoid: No injury, punishment, rope around the neck, distress or falling motion.

death.name: Death
death.gesture: A quiet armored rider on a pale horse moves at a solemn walking pace past a permanently sealed old gate while carrying one lowered black banner marked only by a single white rose; dawn rises between two distant pillars.
death.dominantSymbol: the pale horse and lowered black banner with one white rose
supportingSymbols: a new dawn between two distant pillars
death.avoid: No corpse, skeleton close-up, gore, weapon attack or disaster; do not soften it into only a seasonal landscape.

temperance.name: Temperance
temperance.retouchInstruction: Remove the large and secondary medium eight-point sky stars and preserve the figure, vessel exchange, palette and all other approved visual properties; the v2 source remains byte-identical history.
temperance.gesture: The traveler stands with one foot on stone and one in shallow water, pouring one continuous stream between two vessels.
temperance.dominantSymbol: water flowing between exactly two vessels
supportingSymbols: one foot in water and one on land
temperance.avoid: No large star or second stream to ground; The Star must use a different two-direction action.

the-devil.name: The Devil
the-devil.gesture: Two adults notice that the loose cords tying them to an imposing horned stone figure can be lifted away by their own hands.
supportingSymbols: a dim workshop threshold opening to daylight
the-devil.avoid: No literal demon claim, nudity, fetish restraint, coercion, flames, gore or cute mascot treatment.

the-tower.name: The Tower
the-tower.gesture: People at a safe distance brace and turn as lightning splits the false upper addition of a tall stone watchtower.
the-tower.dominantSymbol: a lightning-struck tower shedding its unstable crown
the-tower.avoid: No falling bodies, injury detail, firestorm, apocalypse or graphic disaster spectacle.

the-star.name: The Star
the-star.gesture: In an open natural clearing, the astronomer pours from two vessels at once, one stream returning to a pool and the other nourishing bare ground.
the-star.dominantSymbol: one large eight-point star with seven smaller stars
supportingSymbols: two vessels feeding land and water
new plants at the ground stream
the-star.avoid: No observatory, building, single vessel or Temperance-style vessel-to-vessel stream.

the-moon.name: The Moon
the-moon.gesture: The traveler pauses before a winding night road between two boundary towers while a domestic dog and a wild wolf watch from opposite sides.
the-moon.dominantSymbol: a large veiled moon above an uncertain road
the-moon.avoid: No observatory, star field, confident forward stride or horror animals.

the-sun.name: The Sun
the-sun.gesture: Two children run openly through a sunflower courtyard, fully lit and unguarded, while an adult watches from a respectful distance.
the-sun.avoid: No horse, naked child, celestial star field or decorative extra suns.

judgement.name: Judgement
judgement.gesture: A diverse group rises from rest and turns toward a high civic bell, answering its call with alert, accountable expressions.
judgement.dominantSymbol: a high bell sounding across an opening square
supportingSymbols: opened unlabeled record boxes with no visible writing or marks
judgement.avoid: No graves, corpses, literal resurrection, angelic truth claim or religious insignia.

the-world.name: The World
the-world.gesture: The gardener moves alone in a balanced dance within a complete living wreath, holding two short ribbons in a clean centered silhouette.
supportingSymbols: four distinct corner guardians carved in stone
the-world.avoid: No exposed nudity, floating icon collage, large star or incomplete wreath.

wands-ace.name: Ace of Wands
wands-ace.gesture: At sunrise the traveler discovers and firmly lifts one living wooden staff newly sprouting from a dry stone terrace.
supportingSymbols: new green shoots at the terrace
wands-ace.avoid: No other branch, pole, fence post or floating hand.

wands-2.name: Two of Wands
wands-2.gesture: The maker studies a folded route cloth showing only broad unlabeled terrain color fields at a high parapet, holding one staff while a second stands in a stone socket.
wands-2.dominantSymbol: exactly two wooden staffs framing a distant route
supportingSymbols: a folded route cloth with no visible writing, numerals or symbols
wands-2.avoid: No globe, extra railing posts or active departure; keep it distinct from Three of Wands.

wands-3.name: Three of Wands
wands-3.gesture: The traveler stands beside three planted staffs and watches a small trade caravan returning along the valley road.
wands-3.avoid: No map, ocean ship or fourth pole; show progress already under way.

wands-4.name: Four of Wands
wands-4.gesture: Neighbors meet beneath a simple harvest canopy built from four staffs, greeting each other after completing a shared stage.
wands-4.dominantSymbol: exactly four wooden staffs forming a stable canopy
wands-4.avoid: No wedding symbolism, paired-path Lovers composition or extra canopy poles.

wands-5.name: Five of Wands
wands-5.gesture: Five participants cross five practice staffs in a lively training exercise, each aiming differently without striking a body.
wands-5.avoid: No violence, injury, identical faces or sixth staff; keep the conflict energetic but safe.

wands-6.name: Six of Wands
wands-6.gesture: A returning rider carries one laurel-tied staff while companions walk with five more, acknowledging completed work without worship.
wands-6.dominantSymbol: exactly six wooden staffs led by one laurel-tied staff
wands-6.avoid: No chariot, triumphal crown or seventh staff.

wands-7.name: Seven of Wands
wands-7.gesture: The gardener braces one staff across a narrow high gate while six staffs rise from people below, defending a boundary without attack.
wands-7.dominantSymbol: exactly seven wooden staffs at two elevations
wands-7.avoid: No cliff fall, injury or eighth pole; show boundary defense rather than conquest.

wands-8.name: Eight of Wands
wands-8.gesture: Eight wooden staffs travel in one clean diagonal through the air after a coordinated release across an empty training field.
wands-8.dominantSymbol: exactly eight parallel moving wooden staffs
wands-8.avoid: No people under the staffs, impact, floating icon grid, fence or ninth pole.

wands-9.name: Nine of Wands
wands-9.gesture: A tired traveler with a simple head wrap leans on one staff while eight more form a repaired barrier behind, still alert but not fighting.
wands-9.dominantSymbol: exactly nine wooden staffs: one held and eight behind
wands-9.avoid: No bleeding wound, tenth pole or aggressive opponent.

wands-10.name: Ten of Wands
wands-10.gesture: One worker carries a clearly separated bundle of ten staffs toward a store yard, posture strained while another person offers to share the load.
wands-10.avoid: No hidden eleventh staff, punishment or collapse; make the burden readable at thumbnail size.

wands-page.name: Page of Wands
wands-page.gesture: Seen from above at a close three-quarter angle, the traveler kneels on a practice cloth and tests the balance and leather grip of one fully seasoned staff, visibly curious and attentive.
wands-page.dominantSymbol: exactly one finished wooden staff being tested for balance
supportingSymbols: a blank practice cloth with no visible writing or marks
wands-page.avoid: No sprout, dog, cliff, departure stride, notebook or second branch; keep it distinct from The Fool and Ace of Wands.

wands-knight.name: Knight of Wands
wands-knight.gesture: Seen from a low three-quarter view, moving left to right, the maker rides a single chestnut horse across a dry rise, holding one staff upright while visibly checking speed before a turn.
wands-knight.dominantSymbol: exactly one wooden staff in controlled forward motion
wands-knight.avoid: No chariot, paired horses, reckless rear, flames or second staff.

wands-queen.name: Queen of Wands
wands-queen.gesture: The gardener confidently coordinates an outdoor work circle with one staff used as a speaking token, welcoming input without surrendering direction.
wands-queen.dominantSymbol: exactly one wooden staff held with relaxed confidence
supportingSymbols: a natural black cat seated apart
wands-queen.avoid: No crown, throne, lion or second staff; show leadership through action rather than gender.

wands-king.name: King of Wands
wands-king.gesture: The elder steward stands over a physical scale model of a long-term camp, using one staff to indicate the next practical milestone to a prepared team.
wands-king.dominantSymbol: exactly one wooden staff directing a sustainable plan
supportingSymbols: a finished physical route model with no writing or marks
wands-king.avoid: No throne, crown, Emperor seat or extra map poles; authority is a role, not gender.

cups-ace.name: Ace of Cups
cups-ace.gesture: At dawn one empty cup rests at the center of a spring ledge as fresh water rises into it and gently overflows.
cups-ace.dominantSymbol: exactly one handled cup receiving fresh water
cups-ace.avoid: No hand, second vessel or vessel-to-vessel pouring; keep it distinct from Temperance and The Star.

cups-2.name: Two of Cups
cups-2.gesture: Two people meet at a small table and exchange two cups at equal height while making clear mutual eye contact.
supportingSymbols: a reciprocal handover witnessed at equal height
cups-2.avoid: No open-hand garden threshold, third person or third cup; distinguish it from The Lovers.

cups-3.name: Three of Cups
cups-3.gesture: Three friends raise three cups in a loose circle after finishing a shared task, each face and hand distinct.
supportingSymbols: a simple shared meal with no other vessels
cups-3.avoid: No fourth cup, identical faces, intoxication or romantic-couple framing.

cups-4.name: Four of Cups
cups-4.gesture: A tired traveler sits beneath a courtyard tree before three cups while a neighbor quietly sets down a fourth within reach.
cups-4.dominantSymbol: exactly four cups: three together and one newly offered
cups-4.avoid: No floating hand, fifth cup or dramatic rejection; show disengagement rather than ingratitude.

cups-5.name: Five of Cups
cups-5.gesture: A grieving figure acknowledges three spilled cups on a rain-dark courtyard while two upright cups remain behind within sight.
cups-5.dominantSymbol: exactly five cups: three spilled and two upright
cups-5.avoid: No blood, death scene, hidden sixth cup or forced optimism.

cups-6.name: Six of Cups
cups-6.gesture: An older neighbor and a child carefully exchange one flower-filled cup while five more mark familiar places in an old courtyard.
cups-6.avoid: No romantic framing, nostalgia haze, seventh cup or claim that the past must be restored.

cups-7.name: Seven of Cups
cups-7.gesture: The maker compares seven cups arranged on uneven alcove shelves, each holding one different practical or fanciful option.
cups-7.dominantSymbol: exactly seven cups containing distinct choices
supportingSymbols: one blank decision cloth with no visible writing or marks
cups-7.avoid: No floating cloud collage, eighth vessel or horror object; keep the options physical and countable.

cups-8.name: Eight of Cups
cups-8.gesture: At dusk the traveler leaves eight carefully stacked cups on a low wall and walks toward a quiet inland path.
cups-8.dominantSymbol: exactly eight stacked cups being left intact
cups-8.avoid: No ninth cup, spilled vessels, cliff edge or Fool-like joyful stride.

cups-9.name: Nine of Cups
cups-9.gesture: Seen in a close three-quarter interior view, a host finishes placing the ninth cup onto a freestanding three-tier wooden serving stand after completing a modest community feast.
cups-9.dominantSymbol: exactly nine cups on one freestanding three-tier display
cups-9.avoid: No wall niche, alcove shelf, tenth cup, excess food, smug caricature or crown.

cups-10.name: Ten of Cups
cups-10.gesture: Seen in a wide outdoor view, a chosen family places the final cup onto a long straight communal table where exactly ten cups form one even row after setting a shared home in order.
cups-10.dominantSymbol: exactly ten cups arranged in one straight row on a long communal table
cups-10.avoid: No curved shelf, rainbow made of cups, extra tableware, idealized nuclear-family stereotype or eleventh cup.

cups-page.name: Page of Cups
cups-page.gesture: The maker holds one cup at eye level and looks with amused curiosity at a small fish briefly peeking from the water inside.
cups-page.avoid: No second vessel, magical glow, childish anatomy or literal message scroll.

cups-knight.name: Knight of Cups
cups-knight.gesture: Seen in a medium-distance side profile moving right to left, the gardener rides a pale horse at a careful walking pace beside the river, carrying one cup level with both attention and restraint.
cups-knight.dominantSymbol: exactly one cup carried steadily in motion
cups-knight.avoid: No raised staff, chariot, gallop, second cup or romantic rescuer pose.

cups-queen.name: Queen of Cups
cups-queen.gesture: The elder steward sits near the tide line, holding one lidded cup and listening fully to a neighbor seated at equal height.
cups-queen.dominantSymbol: exactly one carefully held lidded cup
cups-queen.avoid: No throne, crown, star chart, second vessel or passive mystic stereotype.

cups-king.name: King of Cups
cups-king.gesture: The traveler, now a practiced harbor steward, holds one cup while calmly coordinating help during rough water from a stable stone platform.
cups-king.dominantSymbol: exactly one cup kept level amid emotional weather
cups-king.avoid: No throne, crown, rescue fantasy, second cup or gender-coded authority.

swords-ace.name: Ace of Swords
swords-ace.gesture: One upright sword stands secured in a stone review table at first light while two open paths become clearly visible beyond.
swords-ace.avoid: No hand, second blade, scales or victory crown; keep it distinct from Justice.

swords-2.name: Two of Swords
swords-2.gesture: A seated decision-maker holds two swords crossed but lowered, eyes covered loosely while listening to wind and water before choosing.
supportingSymbols: a removable cloth over the eyes
swords-2.avoid: No scales, upright Justice pose, third blade or dangerous edge near the body.

swords-3.name: Three of Swords
swords-3.gesture: A grieving person mends a rain-darkened red cloth emblem while three swords rest crossed on a separate rack behind it.
swords-3.dominantSymbol: exactly three swords against a red crafted emblem
swords-3.avoid: No anatomical heart, blood, penetration, body wound or fourth blade.

swords-4.name: Four of Swords
swords-4.gesture: Seen in a wide afternoon exterior, a fully clothed traveler sits upright and still on a stone bench beneath an open shelter, eyes closed and hands relaxed, while four sheathed swords lie side by side on one low rectangular cloth before the bench.
swords-4.dominantSymbol: exactly four sheathed swords resting side by side on one low cloth
swords-4.avoid: No lying figure, sword rack, planted blade, bed, wall-mounted blade, tomb, corpse, injury, medical scene or fifth blade.

swords-5.name: Five of Swords
swords-5.gesture: After a nonviolent contest, one participant gathers three swords while two others each carry one away with dissatisfied expressions.
swords-5.dominantSymbol: exactly five steel swords divided three, one and one
swords-5.avoid: No wounds, blood, gloating caricature, abandoned extra blade or sixth sword.

swords-6.name: Six of Swords
swords-6.gesture: A ferryperson guides two passengers across calm water while six swords remain securely upright in a closed rack at the bow.
swords-6.dominantSymbol: exactly six secured swords moving across water
supportingSymbols: water changing from rough to calm
swords-6.avoid: No exposed blade near passengers, seventh sword, escape panic or funeral mood.

swords-7.name: Seven of Swords
swords-7.gesture: A cautious planner carries five sheathed swords away from a camp while two remain in a rack, repeatedly looking back at the incomplete plan.
swords-7.dominantSymbol: exactly seven swords: five carried and two left
supportingSymbols: an unfinished physical camp model with no writing or marks
swords-7.avoid: No racialized thief stereotype, violence, eighth blade or triumphant expression.

swords-8.name: Eight of Swords
swords-8.gesture: A loosely blindfolded person stands within eight widely spaced grounded swords, hands unbound and a clear gap visible behind.
swords-8.dominantSymbol: exactly eight swords forming an incomplete boundary
swords-8.avoid: No bound body, imprisonment claim, injury, ninth blade or hopeless sealed circle.

swords-9.name: Nine of Swords
swords-9.gesture: A wakeful person sits on a bed holding their face while nine sheathed swords line one wall in repetitive shadow at pre-dawn.
swords-9.dominantSymbol: exactly nine sheathed swords in a repetitive row
swords-9.avoid: No self-harm, monster, diagnosis, blood, tenth sword or blades over the bed.

swords-10.name: Ten of Swords
swords-10.gesture: An exhausted worker lies safely on a cloak beside a rack of ten planted swords after closing an abandoned work site, dawn visible beyond.
swords-10.dominantSymbol: exactly ten grounded swords marking a finished line
supportingSymbols: an exhausted but living resting figure
swords-10.avoid: No corpse, blood, penetration, body-contacting blade, eleventh sword or melodramatic attack.

swords-page.name: Page of Swords
swords-page.gesture: The elder learner practices one sword's balance in a windy yard under supervision, feet alert and blade safely angled away.
swords-page.dominantSymbol: exactly one sword being carefully studied
swords-page.avoid: No attack, crown, age stereotype, second blade or Knight-style forward motion.

swords-knight.name: Knight of Swords
swords-knight.gesture: Seen from a tight frontal three-quarter angle moving diagonally toward the viewer, the traveler rides into a hard crosswind on a gray horse, carrying one sheathed sword forward while checking a signal flag ahead.
swords-knight.dominantSymbol: exactly one sheathed sword in urgent movement
swords-knight.avoid: No raised attack blade, battle, chariot, second sword or uncontrolled charge.
